newsitem.title: PERU: Peru plans to light up Machu Picchu ruins.
newsitem.headline: Peru plans to light up Machu Picchu ruins.

text.p: Peru plans to illuminate its famous Machu Picchu ruins with giant solar-powered lights that will allow them to be seen at night, an official said on Thursday.

The lighting will not damage the 700-year-old site, perched spectacularly on the saddle of a mountain on the eastern slopes of the Andes, National Culture Institute director Luis Arista told local news media.

The spotlights, to be powered by solar cells, will be placed outside the ruins, not inside, and will allow visitors "to appreciate the archaeological monument from a certain distance," he said. They will not be allowed to visit the ruins at night, he added.
He said a French company with experience in illuminating world-famous historical sites in Asia and Africa, which he declined to name, had offered a proposal for the project.

About 50,000 people visited the ruined Inca fortress in the first three months of this year, authorities said. One of South America's top tourist draws, it was abandoned at the time of the Spanish conquest and was rediscovered about 1920.
